text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. speaker: Doctor
text: Did you notice any tick bites during your camping trip in Minnesota, and have you observed a circular, expanding rash on any part of your body? I need to know if you've experienced any headache or severe fatigue alongside these symptoms.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain in the left wrist. I also have Chills, Malaise, Painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on both wrists and hands, Swelling and erythema of the left wrist, Severe tenderness to palpation and passive movement of the left wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have any sensitivity to sunlight, and have you noticed any joint pain in other areas besides the wrist and previous knee issue? I am considering a diagnosis of disseminated gonococcal infection given your sexual history and specific skin lesions.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Otherwise healthy with no significant past medical history. Social history: Admits to being sexually active with one female partner who uses a diaphragm for contraception. Recently went on a camping trip to Minnesota.

speaker: Doctor
text: I will perform a joint aspiration of the left wrist to analyze the synovial fluid for cell count, Gram stain, and culture to confirm the suspected disseminated gonococcal infection. REQUEST TEST: Synovial Fluid Analysis.
